children.counts: Two sways left, two sways right per bar.
children.game_version: A mirror-sway game where children hold hands in pairs and sway together to a slow count.

seniors.seated_version: Perform the upper body sway and arm movements while seated in a stable chair.
seniors.standing_version: Stand with feet hip-width apart and practice the gentle weight shifts and body sways without a partner.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduced range of motion, maintaining a very slow tempo.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: One arm embracing the partner, while with the other arm they hold hands
movement_profile.partnering: Couples dancing closely with an arm embrace and hand hold

signature_moves.description: Swaying the body twice to one side for one musical bar, then twice to the opposite side on the next bar.
signature_moves.name: The Two-Bar Body Swing

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Lento (slow) or andante depending on regional variant

music_profile.musical_form: Strophic alternating with a refrain, featuring a solo instrumental intro and a middle instrumental improvisation
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Syncopated, where a note at the end of a bar is extended to the strong beat of the next; accented on the first and last half-beat
music_profile.sound_description: A slow, plaintive acoustic sound led by guitar fingerpicking (*mãozada*) intertwining a steady bass with arpeggiated chords, accompanied by expressive, sorrowful vocals exploring themes of longing and departure.
music_profile.vocal_style: Emotional, lyrical, sung in Cape Verdean Creole

basic_steps: Embrace partner with one arm and hold hands with the other
Sway the body twice to one side during the first musical bar
Shift and sway the body twice to the opposite side during the second musical bar
teaching.level_notes: Beginner friendly, focusing on partner connection and synchronized swaying to a slow tempo.
